svg.title: From Auction Record to Recovery Claim
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-find-verify-contact-document-track; chapter number: 1; title: From Auction Record to Recovery Claim; subtitle: Connect the sale, the available funds, the entitled claimant, and the holding office's requirements.; caption: Ted Thomas describes narrowing auction results to excess proceeds. Eric Richardson of Money Making Juggernaut emphasizes county procedures, while Bob Diamond emphasizes identity and agreements.; assumptions note: Richardson's accessible-county approach requires knowing the local claim process. Diamond's agreement examples are not universal filing requirements.; note: SurplusFundsRiches warns that old balances may already be claimed. Diamond identifies signing the wrong person as a recurring failure.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Find sold-auction candidates; value: Step 1; detail: Ted Thomas starts with auction results and narrows to properties sold for more than the county originally asked.; step: 02; label: Verify funds and competing debt; value: Step 2; detail: SurplusFundsRiches checks list age, continuing availability, ownership, and debt as they stood at the sale.; step: 03; label: Locate the entitled claimant; value: Step 3; detail: Richardson uses locating research and repeatable outreach. Diamond checks that the person is the intended claimant rather than a relative or namesake.; step: 04; label: Agree and assemble documents; value: Step 4; detail: Diamond describes a fee agreement, power of attorney, assignment, and payment direction. Richardson first establishes how the selected county accepts claims.; step: 05; label: Submit and track the claim; value: Step 5; detail: Richardson follows the county's filing route. Unclaimed CEO identifies the actual holding office and timing, while Diamond warns against discovering deadlines after signing.
